## B — Audience, Pavement markings, Michigan Lefts and traffic signals

The audience is first-time, never-licensed applicants for a Michigan operator's license, reading at a plain-English level, plus newcomers and parents of teen drivers who use the same handbook. This section covers white and yellow pavement lines, crosswalk and stop lines, directional arrows, bicycle and shared lane markings, the left-turn-only center lane, Michigan Lefts, yield lines, traffic signal colors, the doghouse signal, flashing signals, the flashing yellow arrow left-turn signal, pedestrian signals and the Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon. It teaches what each line color and pattern allows, how to drive a Michigan Left, what every steady, flashing and arrow signal requires, and how pedestrian signals work. It assumes no prior driving knowledge and no prerequisites beyond literacy, so wording stays concrete, procedural and free of legal jargon throughout.
